scaleBasis: Bottom printed dimension 7914 mm between central living side-wall centrelines near original pixels (574,997) and (886,997), a 312 px span: 791.4/312 = 2.5365384615 cm/px, applied uniformly. Raster endpoint placement is approximate.
assumptions: Traced manually from the original 1536 x 1146 raster with x right and y down. Uniform transform: world cm = (source px - (206,72)) * (791.4/312); no independent x/y fit.

The legible bottom dimension 7914 is interpreted as millimetres across the central living span, wall centres near source x=574 and x=886. Endpoints and raster blur introduce several pixels of uncertainty; centimetre values are not survey measurements.

Wall heights are editable 280 cm defaults. Wall thicknesses are white-model approximations (20 cm exterior, 12 cm interior); the thick pier around the left bathrooms is simplified rather than traced as furniture or a room.
Windows omit type, height and sill; semantic-white-model supplies floor-to-ceiling fixed glass following wall height. This is a presentation default, not source evidence of glazing height or style.
All doors use the ordinary editable default, including broad double-leaf and balcony glazed-access spans. Door style, leaf count and swing are not asserted by the white model.
Thin double-line outer balcony boundaries n23/n29/n30 are kept as 110 cm low barrier approximations, not full-height room walls. Their actual railing/parapet construction and height are unknown.
Large white voids above the central passage and between the two southern wings are exterior voids and are preserved. No rooms, infill partitions or furniture have been invented for them.

The large opening d04 at the kitchen/dining boundary may instead be internal glazing or a sliding panel; confidence is reduced. The long i27 and short i28 thin-line interruptions are treated as internal glazing; whether they are operable access panels is uncertain.

Blue branding obscures the central entry and bathroom D. The entry span and bathroom-D door/one toilet are lower-confidence traces. Small shower-screen lines and uncertain bathroom fittings are omitted rather than promoted to walls.

The lower-right copyright overlaps the large-room southern boundary. A continuous wall n21 follows the visible boundary endpoints, but possible glazing there is omitted; review this edge in the editor.

Furniture footprints are rectangular semantic blocks measured approximately from visible symbols. Heights, construction, exact identities and styles are estimates; no catalog models are inferred. The kitchen sink/cooktop intentionally overlap their counter.

Small rugs, bedding, plants, decorative objects, text, dimensions, swing arcs and unclear fixtures are omitted. Slight near-collinear raster offsets and the short left-bathroom pier step are regularized to common junctions.
A thin-line interruption on bathroom A left wall i05 around source y=154..186 is modeled as ordinary door d18 after enlarged source-overlay review; its exact operation is unclear.
limitation: Structural checks and registration consistency do not certify source-image accuracy.
